inlines.v: BLUB'BER, noun [See Blobber, Blob and Bleb.] 1. A blobber, or bubble; a common vulgar word, but legitimate. 2. The fat of whales and other large sea animals, of which is made train-oil. It lies immediately under the skin and over the muscular flesh. 3. Sea nettle, or sea blubber the medusa. BLUB'BER, verb intransitive To weep in such a manner as to swell the cheeks. If I mistake not, this word carries with it the idea of weeping, so as to slaver. BLUB'BER, verb transitive To swell the cheeks or disfigure the face with weeping.
